{{technical|date=June 2016}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:''p''-curvature}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], '''{{mvar|p}}-curvature''' is an invariant of a [[connection (mathematics)|connection]] on a [[coherent sheaf]] for [[Scheme (mathematics)|schemes]] of characteristic {{math|''p'' > 0}}. It is a construction similar to a usual [[Riemann curvature tensor|curvature]], but only exists in finite characteristic.

==Definition==
Suppose ''X/S'' is a [[smooth morphism]] of schemes of finite [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] {{math|''p'' > 0}}, ''E'' a vector bundle on ''X'', and <math>\nabla</math> a connection on ''E''. The '''{{mvar|p}}-curvature''' of <math>\nabla</math> is a map <math>\psi: E \to E\otimes \Omega^1_{X/S}</math> defined by
:<math>\psi(e)(D) = \nabla^p_D(e) - \nabla_{D^p}(e)</math>
for any derivation ''D'' of <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math> over ''S''.  Here we use that the ''p''th power of a derivation is [[freshman's dream|still a derivation]] over schemes of characteristic {{mvar|p}}.
A useful property is that the expression is <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-linear in ''e'', in contrast to the Leibniz rule for connections. Moreover, the expression is ''p''-linear in ''D''. 

By the definition {{mvar|p}}-curvature measures the failure of the map <math>\operatorname{Der}_{X/S} \to \operatorname{End}(E)</math> to be a homomorphism of [[restricted Lie algebra]]s, just like the usual [[Riemann curvature tensor|curvature]] in [[differential geometry]] measures how far this map is from being a homomorphism of [[Lie algebra]]s.
